decisions.decision: Select strict completion rules for Exit 3 recovery.
decisions.authority:
At accepted `main` source state `cee78cff84618c6a5be3be99714682f5822c814f`, select the required cross-process recovery contract. It applies to the bounded B16 Entry/Exit DXF-and-manifest pair. The contract can only add an absent member. It keeps no separate temporary record. The output-member count can only increase. A later Level 2 bounded cycle can recompute the exact expected pair. It can create unpublished payloads only in anonymous creation-bound descriptors. It can abandon unpublished work only by closing those descriptors. It can inspect existing final files without getting mutation authority. It can publish only by adding an absent final path without overwrite. The first successful final link ends rollback permanently.

No published final file can be unlinked, renamed, rewritten, truncated, or replaced. Authentication or path verification gives no deletion authority. POSIX path deletion has no atomic condition for an expected inode. After a publication failure, preserve all published final files. This requirement includes an exact partial or complete output pair. A later command invocation can add only an absent exact counterpart. Report success only after independent validation of the complete exact final pair.

A mismatch, non-regular final file, symbolic link, collision, replay, substitution, inconsistency, ambiguity, or unsupported primitive causes a fail-closed result. Do not remove foreign or uncertain destination state. The diagnostics `cleanup_complete`, `recoverable`, and `destination_changed` must describe the retained state. Related diagnostics have the same requirement. `recoverable=True` is permitted only after independent validation of an exact zero-member, partial, or complete destination. The destination must also have safe retry or authority to add the remaining member. An ambiguity, mismatch, durability uncertainty, or unsupported primitive keeps the destination non-recoverable.

Each successful addition requires `destination_changed=True`. On a failed command invocation, a surviving published final requires `cleanup_complete=False`. These controls do not change: identical complete-pair reuse, repeatable filenames and bytes, manifest schema, contract IDs, and the two-file layout. No-overwrite behaviour and `reuse-identical-or-fail` collision refusal also do not change. One exact regular partial member can now be completed. It is not treated as a collision. Phase 6 remains 1/5 and Exit 3 remains Pending. It needs implementation, focused interruption and recovery evidence, and a new Level 3 panel.
decisions.exclusions:
This decision changes no product code. It does not mark Exit 3 or another exit `Evidenced` or owner-accepted. It gives no production, physical-output, `project-cleared`, equivalence, GUI, or person-workflow authority. It gives no wider-family, performance, legacy-retirement, packaging, or release authority. It changes no risk state.

It does not authorise unlink, rename, rewrite, truncation, or replacement after publication. It does not authorise rollback that uses a path. It does not authorise reading or deletion of existing controls. It does not authorise mutation of foreign or uncertain destination state. Equality, metadata, or path verification gives no deletion authority. This decision does not change output names, bytes, schema, layout, contract IDs, result IDs, or the collision-policy value. It does not add a trust service, generic storage framework, or product runtime dependency.

decisions.decision: Define the supported exporter failure model and its evidence limit.
decisions.authority:
At protected-main baseline `d8e2b640da412ec0aff0300cd7344e78cec0048b`, accept a finite and testable exporter failure model. The model covers ordinary Python exceptions and explicit application cancellation. It covers the named and tested `BaseException` cases. It also covers accepted staging, publication, cleanup, and durability failures. It covers D-P6-003 recovery of an exact partial or complete pair during the next command invocation. It covers process termination at the operating system descriptor and advisory-lock limit. It also covers qualified FreeCAD import and host operation in the documented platform and file-system profile.

The model excludes injection of arbitrary asynchronous `BaseException` values between every pair of bytecode instructions. It excludes each unobservable short period during acquisition or transfer of ownership. It also excludes repeated injection during cleanup. An excluded probe is not automatically a problem or a finding that prevents Exit 3. It remains an Exit 3 finding if it proves a violation of a retained required invariant, supported operation, or accepted recovery control.

Preserve each D-P6-003 file-addition, no-overwrite, exact-only, fail-closed, file-preservation, and truthful-diagnostic control. After an abnormal asynchronous interruption, resource release can be uncertain. Preserve the output and close FreeCAD completely. Start FreeCAD again, reopen the project, and inspect the output normally. Then retry through the normal exporter. Starting FreeCAD again restores the process limit. It does not prove destination correctness or authorise destructive recovery. Phase 6 remains 1/5 and Exit 3 remains Pending. A new Level 3 panel must review evidence against this model.
decisions.exclusions: This decision changes no product source or exporter implementation. It changes no public or stored API, schema, manifest, output byte, fixture, railway behaviour, or risk disposition. It gives no production, physical-output, `project-cleared`, equivalence, GUI, or wider-family authority. It gives no persistence, retained exact-geometry, performance, legacy-retirement, packaging, release, or tagging authority. It authorises no helper process, subprocess exporter, service, or external transaction manager. It authorises no product runtime dependency, generic storage framework, or exporter redesign. Starting the application again never permits destructive recovery. Do not delete, overwrite, replace, rename, rewrite, truncate, or manually change an existing output member. This decision does not accept Exit 3.

decisions.decision: Accept the Phase 6 Exit 4 comparison baseline and performance direction.
decisions.authority:
At protected `main` `9169b7e7beec5cf614b8a5284db0f97367728def`, the project owner accepts the PR #50 FreeCAD 1.1.3 series as the comparison baseline. The evidence source state is `f370b029bb4c1ce34987dc025a741185e233df04`. The exact host profile is `linux-x86_64-flatpak-freecad-1.1.3`. The measurement profile is `phase6-transition-edit-validate-export-profile-v1`. The comparison baseline includes the complete Edit, Validate, Export, warm-reuse, correctness, lifecycle, output, and cleanup conditions.

The owner selects one performance hypothesis. The preview sampler calculates 33 stations. It does zero-origin integration for each interior station. One preview batch function can calculate all preview displacement values without repeated integration at each station. The Level 2 product boundary contains the preview sampler. It also contains one preview batch function if necessary. Directly dependent tests and performance evidence are in the same bounded cycle. The change must preserve all stated railway, preview, canonical-state, transaction, persistence, exact-validation, export, diagnostic, and cleanup invariants.

The rule uses 12 paired blocks on the exact 1.1.3 host profile. Six blocks use the comparison baseline first. Six blocks use the exact candidate first. Edit process CPU time must be lower in at least 10 paired blocks. The median paired difference for Edit process CPU time must be negative. Median paired differences for Edit wall time and cold-journey CPU and wall time must also be negative.

The Level 2 cycle must use the no-displacement rule for Validate, Export, cleanup, warm block values, and resource metrics. It must also use this rule for the journey remainder. A metric has a FAIL result if its median paired difference is more than the comparison-baseline MAD. A metric also has a FAIL result if 10 or more paired differences are positive.

Use the same rule for RSS, RSS change, high-water RSS, and high-water RSS change. Use it in each measured stage and the complete journey. All discrete invariant results must equal the comparison-baseline results. All warm-cycle correctness results must be PASS.

The exact candidate must add no work to an unmeasured boundary. This includes process launch, module import, fixture construction, dialog opening, and final document disposal. It also includes other unmeasured Setup or Teardown work. Inspection must show that all new product work occurs during measured Edit. Stop the cycle if inspection does not give sufficient proof.

A product problem, invariant difference, or correctness failure gives FAIL and stops the cycle. Replacement is possible only for `fixture-or-harness-defect` or `environment-or-profile-defect`. The failed attempt must give no comparison measurement. Preserve all attempts and record the failure class before replacement. Record the block sequence before measurements start. Use the same block and recorded sequence for the replacement.

D-GOV-008 authorises one Level 2 performance optimisation for zero-origin integration in the preview sampler. The cycle must use the accepted comparison baseline and comparison rule. A later Level 3 decision must admit the evidence before owner acceptance of Exit 4.

This decision makes no product change. It does not admit the PR #50 comparison baseline or a later result as Exit 4 evidence. It changes no accepted-exit count, risk disposition, compatibility authority, product output, product schema, public API, or release authority. Exit 4 stays Pending. Exits 1 and 5 stay Pending. decisions.decision: Record the D-GOV-008 direction as exhausted and select baseline attribution.
decisions.authority:
At protected `main` `bbc90531813415ca966131351f668256cdca838f`, the project owner records D-GOV-009 after D-GOV-008. D-GOV-008 stays Accepted. It owns the PR #50 comparison baseline, first preview-sampler performance hypothesis, fixed comparison rule, and first Level 2 product boundary.

Preserve the two later Level 2 attempts as retained negative evidence. Exact candidate `6e1a0c755d7872fe631332d4d1ce4330febdd81b` had a FAIL comparison result. Edit CPU was lower in only 9 of 12 paired blocks. Twenty-two metrics had FAIL results. A read-only review found a numerical problem in the length-unbounded fast path. It did not keep the `1.0e-10` mm preview-oracle tolerance across the complete product domain. Its comparison has SHA-256 `044244345ea65b8a5ed99548be8f2f1f9f34537eddf813dbb7f92f9c4696f936`.

The Simpson-polynomial replacement kept supported-domain numerical equivalence and exact large-scale scalar fallback. All 24 samples had PASS validation results. Edit CPU was lower in only 5 of 12 paired blocks. The paired median difference was `+2.923202` ms. The source report gives the exact-candidate median as 10.71% higher after rounding. The fixed result was FAIL. Ten metrics had FAIL results.

Its comparison has SHA-256 `64c167b424fefe604ada0b66deb435eaa32e924ff09c2265a3f9f9569382874b`. Its classification has SHA-256 `f402ef196ef78f287357f5484b47505a31a2799c3e6b2160053b6ae927d3a110`. Its source diff has SHA-256 `73a236a44ce39d4ac8aace714dcac0e4c9f400bf030561718a9c77bf1301ec8b`.

The two results are not improvement evidence or Exit 4 evidence. They are sufficient to stop new product work in the D-GOV-008 direction. Do not make a third preview sampler, polynomial, approximation, derived cache, or other variation of that performance hypothesis. Current measurements do not show sufficient cost outside the D-GOV-008 preview-sampler product boundary.

The next action is a Level 1 baseline-attribution investigation on the accepted FreeCAD 1.1.3 Edit journey. Its bounded scope can report canonical-state work, state-construction work, and preview-sampler construction. It can also report Coin binding, scene-graph replacement, GUI processing, and the unattributed remainder. Report each measurement area when the method permits it. The investigation gives attribution only.

A later explicit Level 3 owner decision is necessary before a new Level 2 optimisation. The decision must use measured evidence from outside the D-GOV-008 preview-sampler product boundary. It must define the bounded product boundary. It must define the comparison rule before product work starts.
decisions.exclusions:
This decision does not change D-GOV-008 or the two retained negative results. It does not change a FAIL result into improvement evidence or Exit 4 evidence. It gives no authority for a third preview sampler, polynomial, approximation, or derived cache. It gives no authority for another variation of the exhausted performance hypothesis. It gives no authority for a new Level 2 optimisation.

It gives no authority to select an exact candidate after the project knows the results. The baseline-attribution investigation must not start in this cycle. Do not change product source or make a performance optimisation. Do not define a product performance budget or change a performance threshold.

Do not run either retained comparison again. Do not accept Exit 4.

Phase 6 stays at 2/5 accepted exits. Exit 4 stays Pending. Exits 1 and 5 stay Pending. Project status stays `unknown`. No risk disposition changes.

decisions.decision: Adopt the simplified single-review STE lifecycle.
decisions.authority:
The authorised protected-main baseline is `54176f5ae0fea1f72743f856fd9251a53d7e1dbf`. Recovery checkpoint `ac5a7d7ae8c6bf72069b802ebe9e929faf27e789` is implementation evidence only. The project owner adopts this lifecycle: author → freeze scope → one Documentation Review → optional exact reviewed correction once → one final deterministic validation → complete or owner stop.

The Documentation Review is the only linguistic conformance review. It returns one complete verdict: `ACCEPT`, `APPROVED_WITH_EXACT_CORRECTIONS`, or `BLOCKED`. For `APPROVED_WITH_EXACT_CORRECTIONS`, the reviewer supplies all exact replacement wording in the same review. The implementing agent applies those corrections once against verified preimages. The agent invents no other canonical prose and runs no second Documentation Review.

Final deterministic validation proves source identity, exact candidate identity, frozen review scope, receipt, review-state, and final-content identity. It also proves that no unreviewed mutation occurred. It does not independently judge linguistic conformance. A remaining linguistic or semantic failure returns to the owner. A remaining identity or frozen-review-scope failure also returns to the owner.

Untouched legacy documents receive no review. The first material edit of an unreviewed legacy document causes one complete-document review. After acceptance, Git derives materially changed complete logical units from the accepted document identity. Review covers only those units. Unchanged accepted canonical prose receives no further review. Durable review state stays at document level. The verified Issue 9 retrieval architecture and derived cache remain the source-reading route. They do not narrow the applicable Issue 9 requirement set.

The owner authorises only minimum canonical and skill alignment and the Level 3 record. The owner also authorises exact-candidate freeze and the single Documentation Review. The owner authorises one approved exact-correction application and one final deterministic validation. At D-GOV-015 acceptance, the owner also authorised the existing publication-policy non-linguistic independent review. D-GOV-017 later supersedes that one clause for governance-document prose: final deterministic validation ends its document-review cycle, and publication or CI can only verify the final bytes. If all required checks have PASS results, the owner authorises one draft pull request. The owner gives no merge authority.
decisions.exclusions:
